nodes.label: Pentester — Kali WSL
nodes.notes: Authorized engagement (owner: mrr3b00t007). Starts with ZERO credentials, only network reach to 10.0.0.0/24.

nodes.label: Recon & enum
nodes.notes: nmap: unatco.local = AD forest, 2 DCs, AD CS on DC-01. Anonymous LDAP/SMB denied, SMB signing required. Kerberos user-enum found valid accounts; no AS-REP-roastable users; password spray found nothing.

nodes.label: PetitPotam (unauth)
nodes.notes: MS-EFSR EfsRpcOpenFileRaw coercion (T1187). Works with a null session against the unpatched DC — no credential required.

nodes.label: DC-02
nodes.notes: Second domain controller (10.0.0.182). Coerced into authenticating to the attacker as its machine account DC-02$.

nodes.label: ntlmrelayx (10.0.0.226)
nodes.notes: Relay listener. Coerced auth reaches it via a pre-wired portproxy 10.0.0.226:445 -> WSL. Duplicate targets (-tf) let it skip the anonymous session and relay the real DC-02$ auth.

nodes.label: AD CS /certsrv (ESC8)
nodes.notes: AD CS Web Enrolment over HTTP with NTLM and no EPA (ESC8). The relayed DC-02$ auth enrols a certificate.

nodes.label: DC-02$ cert (.pfx)
nodes.notes: Certificate issued for DC-02$ via the DomainController template (relayed enrolment). 'GOT CERTIFICATE! ID 8'.

nodes.label: DC-02$ NT hash
nodes.notes: certipy auth -> PKINIT TGT -> UnPAC-the-hash. NT hash 82a3c669d9cfc4a93e9a56a2b22ed7dd.

nodes.label: DCSync (DRSUAPI)
nodes.notes: DC-02$ is a domain controller, so it holds replication rights (T1003.006). Authenticate as DC-02$ and replicate secrets.

nodes.label: DC-01 (AD CS CA)
nodes.notes: Primary DC and Enterprise CA (unatco-DC-01-CA, 10.0.0.181). Replication source for DCSync.

nodes.label: Administrator hash
nodes.notes: Domain Admin credential recovered via DCSync. NT hash cbd633ce5809d73ab9cf2189dcce3b29.

nodes.label: C:\flag.txt — DC-01
nodes.notes: Flag written and read back via pass-the-hash wmiexec. 2026-09-23 07:36.

nodes.label: C:\flag.txt — DC-02
nodes.notes: Flag written and read back via pass-the-hash wmiexec. Objective complete on both DCs.

steps.note: Authorized internal pentest of unatco.local. The attacker is a Kali WSL host on the 10.0.0.0/24 segment with NO credentials — only network reach. Goal: drop a flag on C:\ of the domain controllers.

1 · Recon & enumeration. nmap reveals an AD forest with two DCs and AD CS on DC-01. Anonymous LDAP/SMB is denied and SMB signing is required (good hygiene). Kerberos user-enum finds valid accounts, but there are no AS-REP-roastable users and password spraying finds nothing — no easy credential foothold.

2 · Coercion — no credentials needed. DC-02 is vulnerable to unauthenticated PetitPotam (MS-EFSR, T1187). A null-session EfsRpcOpenFileRaw call forces DC-02 to authenticate to the attacker as its machine account, DC-02$.

3 · NTLM relay to AD CS (ESC8). The coerced DC-02$ authentication is caught by ntlmrelayx (reached via a pre-wired portproxy) and relayed to AD CS Web Enrolment, which runs over HTTP+NTLM with no channel binding. Trick: the DC sends an anonymous session first, so duplicate relay targets (-tf) are used to skip it and relay the real DC-02$ auth.

4 · Certificate theft. The relayed enrolment succeeds and the CA issues a client-auth certificate for DC-02$ (saved as DC-02.pfx). A certificate is a long-lived credential that survives password resets.

PKINIT + DCSync setup. certipy authenticates with the certificate (PKINIT) and recovers the DC-02$ NT hash. Because DC-02$ is a domain controller, it holds directory replication rights — the key to DCSync.
5a · DCSync to Domain Admin. Acting as DC-02$, secretsdump replicates secrets from DC-01 (DRSUAPI, T1003.006) and dumps the Administrator NT hash — full domain compromise.
5b · Impact — objective met. Pass-the-hash as Administrator (wmiexec) writes and reads back C:\flag.txt on BOTH domain controllers. Pwn3d on DC-01 and DC-02.

Full chain: no creds -> PetitPotam coercion -> NTLM relay to AD CS (ESC8) -> DC-02$ certificate -> PKINIT hash -> DCSync -> Domain Admin -> flag on both DCs. Break it with: HTTPS + Extended Protection (EPA) on AD CS enrolment (or disable HTTP/Web Enrolment), patch/limit coercion (PetitPotam), enforce LDAP/SMB signing and channel binding, and tier the CA away from DCs.
